snippet.title: Probability, Statistics, and Statistical Learning | Machine Learning History & Frontier
snippet.description:
History and Frontiers of Machine Learning — Lesson 2

Teach statistical quantities as typed evidence produced by different procedures, not as interchangeable confidence meters. Preserve the disagreements and scope conditions in the source packet.

Learning objectives:
• Distinguish estimation, hypothesis testing, prediction, and generalization by their objects and warrants.
• Explain why likelihood, p-values, held-out error, and generalization bounds are not interchangeable measures of certainty.
• Relate model class, capacity, sample design, loss, and deployment environment to the scope of a learning claim.
• Use negative controls to reject common inferences from fit or benchmark performance to truth, causality, or robustness.

snippet.title: Cybernetics, Computation, and the Birth of Symbolic AI
snippet.description:
Artificial intelligence did not emerge from one unified idea. This lesson maps the overlapping—and sometimes competing—programs of cybernetics, mathematical computation, early neural models, and symbolic AI from the 1940s through the 1970s. It treats later labels cautiously and connects technical proposals to their institutions, machinery, funding, and disputes.

Course: History and Frontiers of Machine Learning
Lesson 1: Cybernetics, Computation, and Symbolic AI

Selected primary and archival sources:
• McCulloch & Pitts (1943), A Logical Calculus of the Ideas Immanent in Nervous Activity: https://direct.mit.edu/books/edited-volume/chapter-pdf/2248320/9780262363174_c000800.pdf
• Dartmouth Summer Research Project proposal: http://jmc.stanford.edu/articles/dartmouth/dartmouth.pdf
• Newell & Simon, The Logic Theory Machine (RAND): https://www.rand.org/content/dam/rand/pubs/papers/2024/P868.pdf
• Rosenblatt, The Perceptron: https://direct.mit.edu/books/edited-volume/chapter-pdf/2248354/9780262363174_c001700.pdf
• Minsky, Steps Toward Artificial Intelligence: http://incompleteideas.net/papers/Minsky60steps.pdf
• Lighthill Report (1973): https://rodsmith.nz/wp-content/uploads/Lighthill_1973_Report.pdf

This is an AI-assisted visual explainer produced from a bounded source corpus. It is educational material; historical interpretation and source challenges are welcome.
